page: The Microsoft Azure D4pls_v5 is an arm64 virtual machine instance belonging to Azure's low-memory general-purpose category. It is built on an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance features no integrated local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data, and does not contain discrete GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks show solid baseline compute capabilities in synthetic workloads. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves average results for both single-core (1822.49) and multi-core (7228.15) workloads. Large-block uncached memory throughput demonstrates stable bandwidth at 50.73 GB/sec read and 28.94 GB/sec write. In contrast, instruction execution across broader application suites lands in lower brackets, including Geekbench single-core at 1065.0 and multi-core at 3480.0, alongside modest scores in database operations (2535.71) and Redis set operations (5.51 million ops/sec). Hardware AES cryptographic acceleration is present, though the architecture omits x86-specific vector extensions.

The hardware configuration delivers dedicated physical core tenancy, avoiding the resource contention common to hyperthreaded virtual machines. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides an economical operational profile for compute-driven processes that do not consume large memory footprints. However, workloads requiring fast local scratch disks will face IOPS bottlenecks over network-attached storage. The D4pls_v5 is primarily suited for ARM-native software compilation, continuous integration build agents, containerized microservices, proxy layers, and lightweight web serving.
description: The Microsoft Azure D4pls_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated physical cores on a 3.0 GHz Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. Featuring a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance provides 8.0 GB of system RAM without bundled local storage or hardware GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles show steady middle-tier performance in synthetic stress-ng compute tests (1822.49 single-core, 7228.15 multi-core) and consistent uncached memory bandwidth, though composite tests like Geekbench and PassMark reflect bottom-quartile metrics common to first-generation Neoverse-N1 implementations. The architecture benefits from dedicated, non-hyperthreaded physical cores that provide execution predictability without multi-tenant thread interference. The absence of local disk requires external storage provisioning. Consequently, the D4pls_v5 is tailored for compute environments with modest memory requirements, including ARM64 software compilation, lightweight container hosting, REST API services, and distributed microservices.
